First, check how you're searching

Before you fix anything, make sure you're seeing what customers see. Google personalizes results, and searching your own business name proves very little: of course it shows up for its own name. Customers don't search your name. They search the job.

  • Open a private/incognito window, or use your phone with location on.
  • Search the way a customer would: "[your service] near me" and "[your service] [your town]". For example, "gutter cleaning near me" or "electrician Taunton MA".
  • Check both the map results (the box with three businesses) and the regular results below it. They're ranked differently.

If you show up for your name but not for the job, the problem is relevance and trust. If you don't show up for your own name, the problem is usually your Google Business Profile itself.

1. You don't have a verified Google Business Profile

Your Business Profile is the listing that appears in the map results, and for many local service businesses it's the biggest single source of calls. If you never created one, or created one but never finished verification, you won't appear in the map results at all. Search for "Google Business Profile", sign in, and either claim your existing listing (Google often creates one automatically) or create a new one. Then finish verification. Nothing else on this list matters much until that's done.

2. Your profile is suspended or duplicated

Profiles get suspended for things like keyword-stuffed business names ("Joe's Plumbing Best Plumber Boston"), a virtual-office address, or edits that look suspicious. Duplicates happen when a listing was created twice, which splits your reviews and confuses Google. If you're signed in and see a suspension notice, follow Google's reinstatement steps and keep your business name exactly as it appears on your truck and invoices.

3. Your categories don't match what people search

Your primary category is one of the strongest signals for which searches you show up in. A landscaper whose primary category is "Contractor" will struggle to show up for "landscaper near me". Pick the most specific primary category that describes your main work, then add secondary categories for other services you really do.

4. Google doesn't know which towns you cover

Service-area businesses can hide their address and list the towns they serve instead. If your service area is blank or only lists your home town, you're unlikely to appear for searches a few towns over. List the towns you actually want work in. Then make sure your website names them too, in plain words, so Google and customers see the same thing.

5. There's no website behind the listing

A profile with no website, or a link to a Facebook page, gives Google very little to work with. Google reads your website to understand what you do and where. A simple page that lists each service, each town and your phone number helps you show up for more searches, and it gives customers a reason to call you instead of the next listing.

That's what an Enoma page is built for: your services, your towns, a tap-to-call button and a quote form that sends requests straight to you. See yours in 30 seconds, built from your Google listing.

6. You have few or no recent reviews

Review count, rating and how recent your reviews are all affect where you rank in the map results, and they affect who gets the call even when you do show up. The fix is unglamorous: ask every happy customer, every time, with a direct link. Our guide on getting more Google reviews has the exact steps and a message you can copy.

7. You're too new, or too far away

New listings take time to build trust, and the map results favor businesses close to the person searching. You can't change where you're based, but you can widen your reach with service pages for the towns you cover and reviews from customers in those towns. Give a brand-new profile a few weeks of steady activity (photos, reviews, posts) before deciding it isn't working.

A 20-minute checklist

  1. Search the job, not your name, in a private window.
  2. Confirm your Business Profile is claimed, verified and not suspended.
  3. Set the most specific primary category, plus real secondary ones.
  4. Fill in your service area with the towns you want work in.
  5. Link a real website that names your services and towns.
  6. Text your last five happy customers your review link.
  7. Add five real photos: truck, team, finished jobs.

Then check again in two to four weeks. Google updates rankings gradually, so don't judge the fix by the next morning's results.

Common questions

Why isn't my business showing up on Google?: common questions

Why does my business show up when I search my name but not my service?

Showing up for your own name only proves your listing exists. To show up for searches like "plumber near me", Google needs to see that you're relevant and trusted for that job in that area: the right primary category, a filled-in service area, a website that names your services and towns, and recent reviews.

How long does it take for a business to show up on Google?

A newly verified Google Business Profile can appear for its own name within days. Ranking for competitive searches like "[service] near me" usually takes weeks to a few months of steady reviews, photos and an accurate website.

Do I need a website to show up on Google Maps?

No, a verified Google Business Profile can appear on Maps without a website. But a listing with a real website behind it gives Google more information about your services and towns, and customers are more likely to call a business they can check out first.

Can I pay Google to show up higher in the map results?

You can't pay to rank higher in the free map results. You can pay for ads, including Local Services Ads, which appear above them. The free results are earned through relevance, distance and reviews.
